Oh wow! After seeing multiple Instagram posts of the macaroon ice cream sandwiches I had to try Ninety's out! I came around 9pm on a Friday and the plaza Ninety's is located in was packed! Inside the shop was busy, but surprising most people were ordering the homemade ice cream. They had about 12 different flavors, but my heart was set on the macaroon sandwich. I looked in the freezer and there had to be 15 different flavors. The ones that popped out the most were pistachio, peanut butter, play dough (cookie dough), birthday cake and strawberry shortcake. My husband and I decided the split the birthday cake macaroon ($5.95). Note they will cut it in half for you and it was easily big enough to split. Ok the sandwich. Wow! The ice cream was cake batter mixed with cake pieces, sprinkles and frosting. And the macaroon was super soft! I thought it would be hard from the freezer, but I was wrong. It was such a perfect mix. Eating the ice cream and macaroon together was so delicious! This was probably one of my favorite ice cream treats Ive ever had. There's also a lake near Ninety's where you can sit or walk around, plus they have paddle boats available. It would be a great little date night to enjoy the paddle boats and go for some Ninety's. I will definitely be back this summer!

Unfortunately, I cannot recommend this place. Granted, we stopped by at 9pm on a Saturday but they are open till 10 so figured we give them a try. My first observation is that in a fridge full of great looking cakes, none of them were covered. What I mean is when you start cutting slices from a refrigerated cake, you MUST cover the exposed inside of the cake with some type of food grade paper or cover to keep it from drying. Out of about 6-7 cakes *none* of them were covered. I thought "these could not possibly be fresh and likely dry and tasting like a fridge". So, decided to skip those. My wife opted for some sort of pastry that had a light cream filling in another cooler cabinet. Wow, I wish we would have taken a bite while at the place because when we did later in the car, we almost lost a couple of teeth. I mean, this thing was hard like a brick, tasted like freezer burn and was insipid. Horrible. Look, I get it that on a Saturday at 9pm I don't expect necessarily for things to have been made the hour before but I have eaten at late night bakeries such as Amelie's and I have never had to throw away something because it was not fresh. At VIllani's they clearly do not care what they are serving late at night. I get that maybe a few pastries would sneak in between the fresh batches but the fact that the cut cakes were completely exposed to the fridge air was proof enough that they simply are not trained in food freshness efforts. Tip to them: Cover your cakes, toss old pastries, and offer better. If the goal is to serve the drunk crowd from plaza midwood, then that may be good enough but not for anyone else.

Poor Overall Performance and Longevity. I bought this in July and began using it in early September. It seemed like it would be easy to use, as well as clean and maintain. The extra features included a beard trimmer, a nose-hair trimmer, and a face brush. There was also a charging cord but no actual charger.

I ended up using this every day for about 100 days before the lid broke for the cutter housing. It broke right where you would expect at the hinge after normal opening and closing for cleaning per the instructions. For what I paid for the shaver, it didn't seem worth it to try and find a replacement cutter housing.

The shave itself is by far the worst I've ever gotten from an electric shaver. I did use it consecutively for more than several weeks to allow my face to adjust. This wasn't the issue as my face was already used to using electric shavers and I had no adjustment period issues with my face. The issue was that the cutters were just plain dull and ineffective. Even with three heads I would say I spent at least twice as long shaving with this shaver as compared to my last one. Though it has three cutting heads, I would sometimes have to make a half a dozen passes over the same area before the stubble was cut flush with my skin.

The shaver seemed to use a lot of charge for a single shave. Enough of a charge that it typically took 4+ hours to fully recharge after a single shave. I'm not sure if it was the battery or the charging cord but the charger was actually the same one I used with the previous shaver with much better results.

The nose hair trimmer worked well. I never used the beard trimmer or facial brush.

Went with the milk tea bun, matcha bun, croquet, taro bun, curry bun & one that had bacon on it. The croquet hit the spot for that savory craving, full of flavor & just the amount of filling. Curry was also good, however I do wish there was some spice to it. The taro bun was so soft & the filling wasn't too sweet. The remaining ones I took home, threw it in the fridge & didn't eat till the next day to which at that point they were 2 days old. I gave a few away, but don't worry, I ate one first to see if it was okay. I decided on the milk tea, zapped it the microwave , good as new. The bun was soft & to my surprise there was actual boba in the filling, of course it was a bit melted but it was still really good like milk tea, & not overly sweet. Since that was safe, I gave the matcha bun to my coworker, who enjoyed it & also commented how she liked it because it wasn't too sweet. Also gave away the bacon & croquet, both of which got positive feedback. I also have to mention that the croquet wasn't consumed till 3 days old & was still good. Everything is individually wrapped, so it's an easy pick up & go. I just had to put some tape on them before packing it in my carry on. This might be my new thing to take home whenever one is nearby. Everything was good & held up well. Can't wait to go back & try more! Yumm, my mouth is watering just thinking about it.
